description: An introduction to homeostasis, covering how the body regulates temperature through vasoconstriction, vasodilation, shivering and sweating, controls blood glucose using insulin and glucagon, and manages water and salt balance through osmoregulation and antidiuretic hormone (ADH).

mcq.questionText: The maintenance of a stable internal environment in the body, despite external changes, is called:
mcq.explanation: Homeostasis is a stable internal environment. Exam Tip: Covers temperature, blood sugar and water balance regulation.

mcq.questionText: The normal core body temperature in a healthy human is approximately:
mcq.explanation: Normal human body temperature is about 37C. Exam Tip: 37C is the standard reference.

mcq.questionText: When the body is too hot, sweat glands produce more sweat, which cools the body mainly through:

options.text: Evaporation of sweat from the skin, which removes heat
Absorption of heat by the sweat

mcq.explanation: Sweat evaporates, using body heat to change liquid to vapour, cooling the skin. Exam Tip: Evaporation requires heat energy, drawn from the skin.

mcq.questionText: When the body is cold, small blood vessels near the skin surface narrow. This process is called:
mcq.explanation: Vessel narrowing is vasoconstriction. Exam Tip: Vasoconstriction reduces heat loss in the cold.

mcq.questionText: When the body is hot, small blood vessels near the skin surface widen, allowing more blood (and heat) to reach the surface for cooling. This is called:
mcq.explanation: Vessel widening is vasodilation. Exam Tip: Vasodilation increases heat loss - cooling effect.

mcq.questionText: Involuntary rapid muscle contractions that generate heat when the body is cold are called:
mcq.explanation: Shivering contracts muscles rapidly, releasing heat. Exam Tip: Shivering is automatic in cold conditions.

mcq.questionText: The maintenance of a constant blood glucose (sugar) level in the body is controlled mainly by hormones from the:
mcq.explanation: The pancreas releases insulin and glucagon. Exam Tip: Pancreas hormones: insulin (lowers), glucagon (raises).

mcq.questionText: The hormone insulin, released when blood sugar is too high, works by:

options.text: Helping body cells absorb glucose from the blood, lowering blood sugar

mcq.explanation: Insulin promotes glucose uptake by cells, lowering blood glucose. Exam Tip: Insulin lowers; glucagon raises.

mcq.questionText: The hormone glucagon, released when blood sugar is too low, works by:

options.text: Causing stored glycogen in the liver to be converted back to glucose, raising blood sugar

mcq.explanation: Glucagon breaks down glycogen into glucose, raising blood sugar. Exam Tip: Glucagon = glucose gone up.

mcq.questionText: The regulation of water and salt balance (osmotic concentration) in body fluids is called:
mcq.explanation: This is osmoregulation. Exam Tip: The kidneys play the main role in osmoregulation.

mcq.questionText: If a person drinks a large amount of water, the kidneys respond by producing:
mcq.explanation: Kidneys remove excess water as more dilute urine. Exam Tip: More water in = more dilute, larger urine volume.

mcq.questionText: If a person is dehydrated (has too little water in the body), the kidneys respond by producing:

options.text: A large volume of dilute urine
A small volume of concentrated urine

mcq.explanation: Kidneys conserve water, producing small concentrated urine. Exam Tip: Dehydration -> small, dark, concentrated urine.

mcq.questionText: Which hormone helps the kidney reabsorb more water when the body needs to conserve it?
mcq.explanation: ADH increases water reabsorption in the kidney. Exam Tip: ADH is released by the pituitary gland.

mcq.questionText: A condition in which the body cannot properly regulate blood sugar, leading to persistently high glucose levels, is called:
mcq.explanation: This is diabetes. Exam Tip: Diabetes results from insufficient insulin or poor response.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an example of homeostasis in the human body?

options.text: Digestion of food in the stomach
Maintaining a constant body temperature around 37C despite outside temperature changes

mcq.explanation: Keeping body temperature steady despite the environment is homeostasis. Exam Tip: Homeostasis = keeping internal conditions stable regardless of external change.

fib.questionText: The maintenance of a stable internal environment in the body is called ____.
fib.explanation: Keeping internal conditions stable despite external changes is homeostasis. Exam Tip: Covers temperature, blood sugar and water regulation.

fib.questionText: The normal human body temperature is approximately ____ degrees C.
fib.explanation: 37C is the standard reference for normal human body temperature. Exam Tip: A very frequently tested number.

fib.questionText: The narrowing of blood vessels near the skin in cold conditions is called ____.
fib.explanation: Narrowing of skin blood vessels in the cold is vasoconstriction. Exam Tip: Reduces heat loss.

fib.questionText: The widening of blood vessels near the skin in hot conditions is called ____.
fib.explanation: Widening of skin blood vessels in the heat is vasodilation. Exam Tip: Increases heat loss, cooling the body.

fib.questionText: Rapid, involuntary muscle contractions that generate heat when cold are called ____.
fib.explanation: Rapid involuntary muscle contractions that produce heat are called shivering. Exam Tip: An automatic response to cold.

fib.questionText: The hormone that lowers blood glucose level is ____.
fib.explanation: Insulin helps cells absorb glucose, lowering blood glucose level. Exam Tip: Released by the pancreas.

fib.questionText: The hormone that raises blood glucose level by converting stored glycogen to glucose is ____.
fib.explanation: Glucagon converts stored glycogen back into glucose, raising blood glucose. Exam Tip: Opposite action to insulin.

fib.questionText: The regulation of water and salt balance in the body is called ____.
fib.explanation: Regulating water and salt balance in the body is osmoregulation. Exam Tip: Mainly carried out by the kidneys.

fib.questionText: The hormone that helps the kidney reabsorb more water is ____.
fib.explanation: Antidiuretic hormone (ADH) increases water reabsorption in the kidney. Exam Tip: More ADH = less urine produced.

fib.questionText: A disorder in which the body cannot properly regulate blood glucose is called ____.
fib.explanation: Failure to properly regulate blood glucose is diabetes. Exam Tip: Linked to insufficient or ineffective insulin.

tf.questionText: Homeostasis is the maintenance of a stable internal environment in the body.
tf.explanation: This is the definition of homeostasis. Exam Tip: A core concept linking temperature, sugar and water regulation.

tf.questionText: Vasoconstriction increases blood flow to the skin surface, increasing heat loss.
tf.explanation: Vasoconstriction narrows vessels and reduces blood flow to the skin, reducing heat loss, not increasing it. Exam Tip: Vasoconstriction narrows vessels, reducing heat loss.

tf.questionText: Sweating helps cool the body through the evaporation of sweat from the skin.
tf.explanation: Evaporating sweat draws heat from the skin, cooling the body. Exam Tip: Evaporation removes heat from the skin.

tf.questionText: Insulin raises the blood glucose level.
tf.explanation: Insulin lowers blood glucose by helping cells absorb it; glucagon raises it. Exam Tip: Insulin lowers; glucagon raises.

tf.questionText: Glucagon causes stored glycogen to be converted back into glucose, raising blood sugar.
tf.explanation: Glucagon triggers the breakdown of glycogen into glucose when blood sugar is low. Exam Tip: Glucagon works when blood sugar is too low.

tf.questionText: A dehydrated person produces a large volume of dilute urine.
tf.explanation: A dehydrated person conserves water, producing a small volume of concentrated urine, not a large dilute volume. Exam Tip: Dehydrated -> small, concentrated urine.

tf.questionText: Antidiuretic hormone (ADH) increases water reabsorption in the kidney.
tf.explanation: ADH acts on the kidney to increase water reabsorption back into the blood. Exam Tip: More ADH = less water lost in urine.

tf.questionText: Shivering is a voluntary action controlled consciously by a person.
tf.explanation: Shivering is an involuntary, automatic response to cold, not a conscious decision. Exam Tip: Shivering is involuntary and automatic.

tf.questionText: Osmoregulation is the regulation of water and salt balance in the body.
tf.explanation: This is the definition of osmoregulation. Exam Tip: The kidney (via ADH) is central to osmoregulation.

tf.questionText: Diabetes is a disorder related to the regulation of body temperature.
tf.explanation: Diabetes is a disorder of blood glucose regulation, not temperature regulation. Exam Tip: Diabetes = blood sugar regulation disorder, not thermoregulation.

summary.correctAnswer: The maintenance of a stable internal environment in the body despite changes outside it.
summary.explanation: It covers regulation of body temperature, blood glucose, and water and salt balance. Exam Tip: Whenever a question mentions the body staying stable inside despite outside change, think homeostasis.

summary.correctAnswer: The narrowing of blood vessels near the skin surface, which reduces blood flow and heat loss in cold conditions.
summary.explanation: It is one of the body's responses that helps keep body temperature from falling too low. Exam Tip: Constriction narrows -> conserves heat.

summary.correctAnswer: The widening of blood vessels near the skin surface, which increases blood flow and heat loss in hot conditions.
summary.explanation: It brings warm blood close to the skin surface so heat can escape, cooling the body. Exam Tip: Dilation widens -> releases heat.

summary.correctAnswer: Rapid, involuntary contraction of muscles that generates heat to warm the body when it is cold.
summary.explanation: It is an automatic response and cannot be controlled consciously. Exam Tip: Shivering = extra heat production from muscle activity.

summary.correctAnswer: The release of sweat from skin glands, which cools the body as the sweat evaporates from the skin surface.
summary.explanation: Evaporation uses heat energy from the skin, lowering body temperature. Exam Tip: Sweating cools mainly by evaporation, not by the sweat itself being cold.

summary.correctAnswer: A hormone released by the pancreas that lowers blood glucose by helping body cells absorb glucose from the blood.
summary.explanation: It is released when blood sugar rises too high, such as after a meal. Exam Tip: Insulin brings sugar levels down.

summary.correctAnswer: A hormone released by the pancreas that raises blood glucose by converting stored glycogen in the liver back into glucose.
summary.explanation: It is released when blood sugar falls too low, such as between meals. Exam Tip: Glucagon brings sugar levels up, opposite to insulin.

summary.correctAnswer: The regulation of water and salt balance (osmotic concentration) in the body fluids, mainly by the kidneys.
summary.explanation: It ensures cells neither gain nor lose too much water. Exam Tip: Osmoregulation keeps water and salt levels balanced.

summary.correctAnswer: A hormone that increases water reabsorption in the kidney, reducing urine volume and conserving body water.
summary.explanation: More ADH is released when the body needs to conserve water, such as during dehydration. Exam Tip: More ADH means less, more concentrated urine.

summary.correctAnswer: A condition in which the body cannot properly regulate blood glucose, resulting in persistently high blood sugar levels.
summary.explanation: It results from insufficient insulin production or the body's poor response to insulin. Exam Tip: Diabetes = a blood sugar regulation disorder.

hoq.questionText: A student plays football under the hot sun; skin becomes flushed and she sweats heavily. Explain both responses using temperature-regulating mechanisms.

options.text: The flushed skin is due to vasodilation (blood vessels widen, bringing more blood and heat to the surface), and sweating cools the body through evaporation - both responses lower body temperature
Both responses raise body temperature further
Neither response is related to temperature control

hoq.explanation: Vasodilation brings warm blood to the surface (flushed skin, heat loss); sweating cools via evaporation. Exam Tip: Vasodilation and sweating work as a team to cool an overheated body.

hoq.questionText: After a sugary meal blood glucose rises then returns to normal; hours later without eating it falls but is also restored. Explain using the two pancreatic hormones.

options.text: After the meal, the pancreas releases insulin, which helps cells absorb the excess glucose, lowering blood sugar to normal; later, when glucose falls, the pancreas releases glucagon, which converts stored glycogen back to glucose, raising blood sugar to normal
The liver has no role in either stage

hoq.explanation: High glucose -> insulin released, cells absorb glucose. Low glucose -> glucagon released, glycogen converted back to glucose. Exam Tip: Insulin and glucagon are a classic antagonistic pair keeping blood sugar steady.

hoq.questionText: Student A drinks 1.5L water and urinates frequently with pale watery urine. Student B works outdoors, sweats heavily, produces small dark concentrated urine. Explain using ADH and osmoregulation.

options.text: Both students will produce identical urine

Student A has excess water in the body, so less ADH is released, meaning less water is reabsorbed in the kidney, producing a large volume of dilute urine; Student B is short of water (from sweating), so more ADH is released, increasing water reabsorption and producing a small volume of concentrated urine
ADH has no effect on urine volume
Student B's kidneys have stopped working

hoq.explanation: Excess water -> less ADH -> more dilute urine (Student A). Water shortage -> more ADH -> more concentrated urine (Student B). Exam Tip: ADH level moves opposite to how much water the body already has.
